question.text: Nucleus <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> is having mass number <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>220</mn></math> and its binding energy per nucleon is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi>MeV</mi></math>. It splits in two fragments <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi></math> of mass numbers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>105</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>115</mn></math>. The binding energy of nucleons in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>MeV</mi></math> per nucleon. The energy <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math> released per fission will be:

solution.text:
The total binding energy of nucleus A is,

EA=220×5.6=1232 MeV

The total binding energy of B and C combined is,

EB+EC=105×6.4+115×6.4=1408 MeV

Therefore, the energy released per fission is,

Q=EB+EC-EA=1408-1232=176 MeV
